name: Bictegravir
route_note: available only in the single-tablet Biktarvy, taken once daily

discovery.note: Unboosted second-generation INSTI structurally related to dolutegravir.

tagline: Integrase inhibitor in Biktarvy, the world's top-selling HIV pill
summary: Bictegravir is a second-generation integrase strand transfer inhibitor that does not need a pharmacokinetic booster. It is available only within Biktarvy, a once-daily single tablet with emtricitabine and tenofovir alafenamide that became the most prescribed HIV regimen in the United States. Like dolutegravir, it has a high barrier to resistance.
mechanism: Bictegravir binds the HIV integrase–viral DNA complex and chelates the active-site magnesium ions, preventing strand transfer of viral DNA into the host chromosome.
It shares much of its resistance profile with dolutegravir, and emergent resistance in clinical trials has been very rare.
uses: HIV-1 infection in adults and children weighing at least 14 kg, as a complete regimen
Switch therapy in virologically suppressed patients, including those with M184V/I

history.title: Phase III results
history.detail: Two phase III trials published in The Lancet show bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF is non-inferior to dolutegravir-based regimens in treatment-naive adults.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Biktarvy is approved in February 2018 after phase III trials against dolutegravir-based regimens; EU approval follows in June.

history.title: Paediatric use
history.detail: The US label is extended to children weighing at least 25 kg.

history.title: Low-dose tablet
history.detail: A low-dose Biktarvy tablet is approved for children weighing 14–25 kg.

history.title: Expanded label
history.detail: The FDA extends the label to people with known or suspected M184V/I resistance.

pk.bioavailability: not established; taken with or without food

safety.boxed_warning: Severe acute exacerbations of hepatitis B in patients co-infected with HBV who discontinue the drug (US label).

facts: Biktarvy was the best-selling HIV medicine worldwide in the mid-2020s, with annual sales above $13 billion in 2024.
Bictegravir is contraindicated with dofetilide and rifampicin.
